description: THERM-110 warning while pack temperature was rising.
Engineer opened the thermal shutdown investigation.
Temperature rose for hours under discharge before the trip. It did not snap back.
THERM-201 opened the contactors. Cooling fan tach was zero.
Device is on 4.2.1, the previous stable image. No 4.3.0 heartbeat signature.
Temperature threshold matches the expected 60 C. This is not a configuration mismatch.
Suspected cooling fan seizure because temperature rose with current and fan tach was zero.
Confirmed cooling fan bearing seizure. The temperature sensor agreed with the rise, so this is not sensor drift.
Fan replacement and recommission procedure issued. Threshold change rejected.
Replacement fan kit issued to the site. The pack stays offline until the fan is installed.
Investigation closed. The pack is still offline pending the physical fan replacement.
COM-214 raised on devices that had just taken 4.3.0.
Compared install time to the first COM-214 on each device.
Latency stepped up at the 4.3.0 install. Signal strength stayed near -64 dBm.
COM-214 and FW-210 share the 4.3.0 heartbeat signature.
4.2.1 uses a fixed heartbeat. 4.3.0 moved timeout handling into the session layer and drops sessions above 120 ms.
Communication timeout values match the approved 30 s setting on the affected devices.
Suspected the 4.3.0 heartbeat change because peers on 4.2.1 did not drop.
Lab test of 4.3.0 reproduced COM-214 at 180 ms induced latency. 4.2.1 did not.
4.3.1 restores 4.2.1 heartbeat timing and keeps compressed frames.
4.3.1 installed on the Cedar Park gateway. Rollback remains in place on the other recovered devices.
Mitigation is in place. Two devices are still on 4.3.0 and the incident stays in monitoring until they move.
INV-360 repeated during the evening discharge.
Opened after the second capped discharge.
Unconstrained shape would have reached the high 80s. Measured power stopped at 75 kW.
CFG-101 matched the cap.
Inverter firmware was not changed during the fault window.
Found Inverter Power Limit parameter_value 75 kW, expected_value 90 kW, status Mismatch.
The 75 kW value explains the flat afternoon peak.
After the value returned to 90 kW the next discharge was no longer capped.
Restore the approved limit and keep the old row for audit.
Running configuration set to 90 kW.
Faults stopped after the configuration correction.
COM-118 gaps started as RSSI fell.
Gateway was offline at the morning check.
From 18:00 on 24 Sep, latency climbed and signal strength fell. Both moved, which is not the 4.3.0 pattern.
COM-101 link loss.
Gateway is on 4.2.1 with no 4.3.0 install. COM-214 was not raised.
Communication timeout is the expected 30 s.
Suspected the radio path because signal strength collapsed with latency.
Confirmed a failed gateway radio path. Distinct from the firmware heartbeat regression.
Radio module replacement procedure.
Replacement radio staged. Gateway has not returned to service in this snapshot.
Cause closed as a radio path failure. Device remains offline until the swap.
First BAT-204 on an HW-C pack.
Second site repeated the same code.
Pack voltage swung between about 705 V and 812 V before the fault. Peers on other revisions did not.
BAT-204 on all three HW-C batteries.
The three packs are not on a shared new firmware image. Hardware revision is the common field.
Current limits match the expected 120 A. Not a configuration mismatch.
Suspected HW-C busbar torque after the common revision and discharge condition lined up.
Confirmed low busbar torque on the HW-C power module.
Torque campaign and a temporary 60 kW discharge cap.
Discharge cap applied. Physical re-torque is not finished.
THERM-110 on a pack whose current was not high.
Warnings repeated without a shutdown.
Temperature climbed smoothly for days and voltage stayed steady. A real thermal mass would not snap back in one sample.
THERM-155 rate-of-change fault.
Firmware matches healthy packs.
Temperature threshold is the expected 60 C.
Suspected the temperature sensor because the rise ignored current.
Confirmed sensor drift. Temperature returned to the high 20s immediately after replacement.
Sensor replacement, not a fan replacement and not a threshold change.
New temperature sensor installed.
False thermal alerts stopped. Pack remained online throughout.
INV-402 at the evening peak.
Output did not recover on the next samples.
Power stepped from about 78 kW to 6.5 kW. Grid frequency did not excursion.
INV-402 with a sagging DC bus.
No firmware change on the day of the drop.
Inverter Power Limit matches 90 kW. This is not the 75 kW mismatch pattern.
Suspected the power module because the bus sagged and the grid did not.
Confirmed a failed inverter power module.
Power module replacement.
Replacement is not installed. The ticket is blocked on the part.
BAT-330 unexpected SOC step.
Opened because the step had no matching energy.
At 03:20 SOC stepped down while battery current and charge/discharge power were near zero. Several explanations still fit.
BAT-330 is the symptom code. It does not name a cause.
Firmware is 4.2.1, the same image as healthy peers. No regression signature.
SOC minimum and maximum match the approved values. The step is not a configuration mismatch.
Hypotheses recorded: estimator bias, current-sensor offset, standby parasitic load. None confirmed.
BAT-340 contactor opened under load.
Same outward symptom as other unexpected shutdowns.
Current fell to zero when the contactor opened. Temperature was normal.
REL-204 coil driver fault. Coil current was zero.
No firmware change in the prior week.
No contactor timing parameter was edited.
Suspected the coil driver because coil current was zero.
Confirmed a failed contactor coil driver. This is not a precharge-resistor failure.
Replace the coil driver.
Driver replaced.
Pack returned to service. Closed after a clean discharge.
Contactor did not close for discharge. Outward symptom matches the 8 Sep event.
Compared with the coil-driver shutdown before assuming the same part.
No DC bus rise during precharge. Temperature was normal.
REL-210 precharge resistor open. Coil current was present, unlike REL-204.
Firmware matches the other pack. Not a firmware split.
Precharge timer matches the expected value.
Suspected the precharge resistor because voltage did not rise.
Confirmed an open precharge resistor. The coil driver from the earlier incident was healthy.
Replace the precharge resistor only.
Resistor replaced.
Pack returned to service. Same symptom as the coil-driver incident, different confirmed cause.
GRID-302 then INV-201.
Output stayed at zero after the grid recovered.
Frequency hit 61.28 Hz and power went to zero. Frequency later returned and power stayed at zero.
GRID-302 excursion followed by INV-201 latch.
No new firmware. Protection behavior matches the spec.
Grid frequency limit matches the expected 0.5 Hz band.
Suspected a real grid excursion because the frequency trace left the band before the latch.
Confirmed a grid frequency excursion and a latched protection trip. The power module is not the failed part.
Supervised reset procedure. No hardware swap.
Watch items crossed the proactive review line.
Opened a monitoring incident so the three signals stay visible.
Temperature is stuck near 40 C, gateway latency is climbing through about 140 ms with stable RSSI, and the third pack shows isolated restarts.
No mismatched limits on the three devices.
